Pip says dreidel. Pop says סְבִיבוֹן (sevivon)! 🌀

The word סְבִיבוֹן comes from סָבִיב (saviv), "around", because it spins around and around. Spin it, say it, and see where it lands! Can your little one say it with Pop? Se-vi-von!

posts.alt_text: Two cartoon speech bubbles, Pip in gold and Pop in sky blue, teach the word gift in English and el regalo in Spanish next to a picture of a wrapped present.
posts.caption:
Pip says gift. Pop says el regalo (el reh-GAH-loh)! 🎁

Who is el regalo for? Shake it, guess, and say it in Spanish with Pop: el re-GA-lo! Fun fact: in Spain, Mexico and much of Latin America, many kids get one more regalo on January 6, el Día de Reyes.

Pip says jelly donut. Pop says סֻפְגָּנִיָּה (sufganiyah)! 🍩

The name is related to סְפוֹג (sfog), "sponge", because the dough is soft and spongy. We fry them in oil on Hanukkah to remember the little jug of oil that lasted 8 nights. Can your little one say it with Pop? Suf-ga-ni-YAH!

posts.alt_text: Two cartoon speech bubbles, Pip in gold and Pop in sky blue, teach the word tree in English and le sapin in French next to a picture of a decorated Christmas tree.
posts.caption:
Pip says tree. Pop says le sapin (luh sah-PAN)! 🎄

Say it with Pop: le sa-PIN, with a soft nasal "in" at the end. Fun fact: Alsace, in eastern France, is famous for some of the oldest Christmas tree traditions in Europe.
